output.headline: TPG is a full-price sponsor with deals in the target's size band, but thin Midwest and sub-sector depth make it a lower-priority call.
output.differentiator: Its median paid of 15.7x is above Advocate Health, Nordic Capital, UPMC and Advent International, and 8 of its 18 deals sit in the target's $100M-$400M size band. [T:record, K:size_band]
output.why_them: Pays full multiples; $100M-$400M deal experience; large capital base

acquirer_overview.title: Large sponsor with an 18-deal, mostly closed record
points: Financial sponsor with 18 deals from 2016 to 2023; 15 of 18 (83%) closed, 17 of 18 (94%) were control deals. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]
Backed by $303.0 billion in assets under management as of December 31, 2025 (TPG Inc.). [P:1]
Provider services are 9 of 18 deals; the rest sit outside it, led by 4 in Health Insurance. [A:angles, K:by_sub_sector]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: A growth-led fit, but without an open platform or Midwest base
points: Growth was a motive in 10 of 18 deals, and the target grows revenue 11.0% with a 16.8% EBITDA margin. [M:high_growth, X:target]
Having bought from this kind of seller is a modest factor in its favour; it has 1 deal in the target's sub-sector and 8 in adjacent provider sub-sectors. [S:own_fit_s, T:record]
Against: Midwest purchase history is a slight negative (1 deal in the region), and it has no open platform for an add-on. [S:geo_fit, T:record, A:angles]

precedent_activity.title: Same-sub-sector and size-band precedents exist, at lower multiples
points: Quality Medical Group: $187M minority investment in the target's own sub-sector, 2022, at 11.2x EV/EBITDA. [D:MA-2022-0350]
Granite Dental Network: $203M platform investment, 2021, at 12.2x. Liberty Addiction Treatment: $118M leveraged buyout, 2021, at 8.8x. [D:MA-2021-0439, D:MA-2021-0369]
Only Midwest precedent is Metro Medical Associates, a $15M SPAC merger in 2018 at 8.8x. [D:MA-2018-0415]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible, but returns at the ask fall short
points: 70 comparable deals show 10.7x to 15.3x EV/EBITDA, median 12.8x; the 75th percentile is defensible as 16.8% margin beats the 12.9% comps median. [V:comps]
TPG's own median paid of 15.7x is above the comparable upper quartile of 15.3x, so it is willing to pay at the top. [V:comps]
IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target; maximum price is $193M at the same exit and $216M at a 15.0x platform exit. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Size and sub-sector depth
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $88M is under half the $200M EV, with just 1 deal in the target's sub-sector. [T:record]
risk_flags.mitigant: 8 of 18 deals fall in the $100M-$400M band; biggest deal was $1,388M. [K:size_band, T:record]
risk_flags.reality: Capacity is proven, but the typical TPG deal is smaller than this target. [T:record]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask is 18.7%, below the 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: The bid needs a platform exit, yet TPG shows no open platform in this sub-sector. [V:lbo, A:angles]

risk_flags.title: Midwest and competitive process
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target's region, and the geography signal works against it. [T:record, S:geo_fit]
risk_flags.mitigant: Growth motive and a $187M same-sub-sector precedent support the case. [M:high_growth, D:MA-2022-0350]
risk_flags.reality: It ranks 9th of 10 on the priority list, behind buyers with deeper Midwest records. [R:rank]

conviction.rationale: Low: one own-sub-sector deal and eight adjacent provider deals support fit, but there is no open platform and the $88M median deal is under half the $200M EV. [C:conviction, T:record]
